title: Check disk integrity with fsck
summary: Use fsck to check the integrity of a disk volume and report any damaged blocks. This command is typically used on unmounted volumes, such as external drives or volumes in Recovery Mode.
prerequisites: The volume you want to check must be unmounted.
You know the device identifier of the volume (e.g., /dev/disk2s1).

steps.explain: Run fsck on the specified device to check its integrity and report any damaged blocks.

warnings: Automatically repairing errors (-fy) can lead to data loss if the filesystem is severely corrupted.
Always back up important data before running repair commands.
The volume must be unmounted; checking a mounted volume can cause data corruption.

rollback.explain: If you accidentally repaired a volume and want to restore it, you must restore from a backup (e.g., Time Machine). fsck itself does not have an undo command.
